entries.title: U.S. stocks slip after the Fed raises interest rates, hints more hikes may be on the way
entries.snippet: U.S. stocks slipped Wednesday after the Federal Reserve hiked its main interest rate for the first time in three years and suggested more may be ahead as it tries to get the nation's high inflation under control.

entries.title: The one issue where Republicans and Democrats are unified before the midterms, according to this poll
entries.snippet: Americans have grown more concerned about the environmental impacts of artificial intelligence over the last year, according to a new poll from The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research and the Energy Policy Institute at the University of Chicago.

entries.title: Trump administration has cut or frozen $177 billion in grants across every state, analysis shows
entries.snippet: Among the grants that were eliminated, frozen or delayed were ones related to maternal health in Michigan, education research in Mississippi and assistance to minority farmers in Iowa, the researchers found.

entries.title: Earth lost more than 12 trillion tons of ice from Greenland and Antarctica in 47 years, satellites show
entries.snippet: A major report has found that 12.5 trillion tons of ice from Greenland and Antarctica have melted since 1979. The massive glacier melt is mainly attributed to warmer waters eroding the ice sheets from below and the sides.

entries.title: Iran war has cost the U.S. more than $38 billion so far, budget office says
entries.snippet: The estimates come largely from replacing munitions and equipment lost in battle, the CBO said, and do not include costs related to U.S. military personnel killed or injured in the conflict or longer term effects.

entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: US Congress passes Russia sanctions bill
entries.snippet: The sanctions package is considered the most substantial US legislative effort against Moscow since Trump returned to the White House. Measures in the bill could lead to secondary sanctions on India, China and Iran.

entries.title: Sweden's center-left bloc set to win election, STV reports
entries.snippet: The center-left opposition won the Swedish elections by a very slim margin, the public broadcaster reported after 99% of the votes were counted. Thorny negotiations await the bloc even if the result is confirmed.

entries.title: US Fed raises key rate for first time in 3 years
entries.snippet: In an attempt to address the persistently high inflation in the world's largest economy, the US Federal Reserve increased interest rates by 25 basis points. The president, on the other hand, said they should be cut.

entries.title: Germany: Oktoberfest beer prices rise, outpacing inflation
entries.snippet: Oktoberfest's traditional beer mug, the Mass, will cost an average of €15.61 ($18.50) at this year's festival in Munich.

entries.title: UK: Village votes to 'secede' in asylum center plan protest
entries.snippet: Residents of Piddington, a tiny, remote village in Oxfordshire in England, have staged a "referendum" on leaving the UK. They are objecting to plans to open an asylum reception center at a disused military base nearby.

entries.title: Can Canada and the EU build a deeper partnership?
entries.snippet: Canadian Prime Minister Carney is known for standing up to US President Donald Trump. Now he wants to forge a "unique alliance" with Europe. But what could such a partnership look like?

entries.title: Chancellor Merz seeks CDU support as AfD encroaches
entries.snippet: Following the CDU's crushing defeat in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, many are expressing doubts about the party's leader, Chancellor Friedrich Merz. But the CDU doesn't appear to have a viable alternative.

entries.title: Shock in Kosovo as Hague convicts former President Thaci
entries.snippet: The conviction in The Hague of former President Hashim Thaci and three former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has caused consternation in Kosovo — both among political leaders and on the streets. DW reports from Pristina.

entries.title: British-American writer Bonnie Greer dies aged 77
entries.snippet: Chicago-born playwright Bonnie Greer, who became a familiar face in British political discourse later in life, has died. Her husband David Hutchins announced news of Greer's death.

entries.title: Gaza: At least 21 dead, including children, in building collapse
entries.snippet: The search for survivors has been hampered by Israeli restrictions on heavy machinery in the Gaza Strip. Authorities say 2,000 damaged buildings in the territory are occupied by families who have nowhere else to go.

entries.title: Forgotten US court of 'secrecy' could mean more deportations
entries.snippet: The use of a secretive and long dormant court in the deportation of a woman from the US could have significant consequences. The Alien Terrorist Removal Court was just used for the first time in its 30-year history.

entries.title: After Neuer: Who will be Germany's new No. 1 goalkeeper?
entries.snippet: Following Manuel Neuer's retirement, there are many candidates to succeed him, but which goalkeeper will Jürgen Klopp choose? What factors will play a role? And will Neuer's future have an indirect influence?

entries.title: How the Houthis are also putting Egypt under pressure
entries.snippet: The Houthis, a Yemeni rebel group, are expanding their control of maritime corridors in the Red Sea area. Their target is their avowed enemy Saudi Arabia. But the military moves also endanger Egypt.

entries.title: Iran: Activists sound alarm as regime seizes Baha'i assets
entries.snippet: Rights groups warn Iran is increasingly confiscating assets from government critics and members of the country's Baha'i faith, but also actors, athletes and journalists living abroad.

entries.title: Poland reaffirms support for Ukraine after drone strikes
entries.snippet: After Russia's recent drone attacks on targets close to the Ukraine-Poland border, Warsaw has doubled down on its support for Kyiv and pledged a "nonprovocative but serious response" to Moscow.

entries.title: Belarus to release 25 more prisoners as US eases sanctions
entries.snippet: Belarus will release 25 more prisoners under an interim agreement with the United States, while Washington plans to lift sanctions on two Belarusian companies and pursue broader negotiations.

entries.title: Congo's Ebola epidemic may have gone undetected for months
entries.snippet: The deadliest Ebola outbreak on record in the Democratic Republic of Congo may have begun months before it was first declared in May.

entries.title: India news: US bill sanctioning Russia could hit India with tariffs of up to 100%
entries.snippet: A new bill could give President Trump the power to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries buying Russian oil and gas, potentially affecting major importer India.

entries.title: Germany news: Conservative state premiers rally behind Merz
entries.snippet: All eight CDU state premiers have backed Friedrich Merz, urging the party to focus on rebuilding trust. Plus, Germany's coalition is weighing rapid relief as record fuel prices pile pressure on households. DW has more.
